title: What If Earth Spun Twice as Fast?

scenes.text: What if Earth spun twice as fast? Your day would last just twelve hours.
Right now the equator moves at about sixteen hundred seventy kilometers an hour. Double that.
Spin pushes water toward the equator, so oceans would pile up there and low coastal cities could go under.
You'd also weigh a little less near the equator, because the spin works against gravity.
Keep speeding up, and at about seventeen times today's speed the equator would become weightless.
Earth really has spun faster. Over four billion years ago, a day may have lasted only four hours.

description:
What if Earth spun twice as fast?
Days shrink to 12 hours, oceans pile up at the equator, and you'd weigh a little less.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Would you like a 12-hour day? What should we run through next?
